name: Aaron Halpern
bio: Bridging complex systems science with practical coordination frameworks to solve collective intelligence challenges.
details:
Aaron leads our strategic initiatives and ecosystem development, bringing formal research expertise through his PhD in systems modeling and complexity science from University College London. His research on self-organizing informational systems produced six published papers and developed novel approaches to understanding how coordination emerges in complex environments.

Beyond academia, Aaron brings business development experience as a cohort member of the Entrepreneur First startup incubator and as an innovation consultant with Zinc, where he focused on open-source projects and fund strategy. As an associate consultant with Outsmart Insight, he advises academic institutions and global businesses on emerging technologies from life-span extension to environmental DNA detection.

His community-building experience includes founding the UCL Biosciences PhD Mentorship Program and organizing over 50 events that bring together diverse perspectives on complex systems challenges.

name: Jonas Hallgren
bio: Developing multi-agent coordination systems that remain stable and aligned even under competitive pressures.
details:
Jonas directs our research architecture and operational systems, drawing from four years of dedicated experience in AI safety research with special focus on multi-agent coordination through active inference frameworks. His technical expertise was refined as Chief Scientific Officer at a Collective Intelligence startup where he developed algorithms for AI agent coordination.

His contributions to AI safety education include curriculum design during his internship at SERI MATS and creating structured research programs like the Distillation for Alignment Practicum and the Alignment Mapping Program. Jonas co-founded AI Safety Sweden (now AI Safety Collab) and helped organize Future Forum, bringing together over 300 participants including industry leaders like Daniella Amodei and Sam Altman.

At Equilibria Network, Jonas designs research architectures that balance theoretical exploration with practical implementation, creating structured environments where complex coordination challenges can be systematically addressed.

name: Markov Grey
bio: Translating complex technical concepts across domains to build resilient coordination systems.
details:
Markov leads our communication strategy and technical infrastructure, combining deep AI safety expertise with the versatility of a technical generalist. His diverse background spans network security, full-stack software development, and blockchain technologies, enabling him to bridge understanding between researchers, practitioners, and policymakers.

His communication experience includes writing AI safety scripts at Rational Animations, serving as a research distillation fellow at AI Safety Info, and researching AI threat models at AI Safety Camp. As research fellow and head of communication at the Center for AI Safety in France, Markov authors an AI safety textbook synthesizing insights from hundreds of research papers, now used in university programs globally including Sorbonne, UBC Vancouver, and École normale supérieure.

Markov's current research focuses on automating alignment research, developing decentralized governance models, and creating frameworks that make collective intelligence concepts accessible across different stakeholder groups.
